vignette: John is a 65-year-old prosecutor who has been married for over forty years. His career as a prosecutor has always demanded unwavering focus and resilience, but recently he finds it increasingly difficult to maintain the composure necessary for his work due to an incident that occurred several months ago. The trauma began during a particularly intense trial where John was prosecuting a case involving police misconduct. After hours of grueling cross-examinations and testimonies, John received news that would forever change how he perceived law enforcement. While leaving the courthouse late one evening, John witnessed what he believed to be excessive force used by two officers against an unarmed civilian who appeared to have been struggling with mental health issues. The incident left him feeling shaken and on edge. Since then, John has found himself replaying the scene over and over in his mind during quiet moments at home or late into the night when trying to sleep. He experiences intrusive thoughts and vivid flashbacks, often feeling like he's back in that parking lot, hearing the sounds of scuffling and shouting. John's wife, Sarah, notices a significant change in him. He is more withdrawn, less communicative about his day-to-day activities, and frequently expresses feelings of anger and frustration towards law enforcement. These emotions have seeped into their household, affecting their relationship dynamics as he becomes easily irritated by minor issues. Even simple mentions of the police or similar authority figures can trigger strong reactions from John. At work, John's performance has started to suffer. He is often distracted during court proceedings, his mind wandering back to the incident he witnessed. This has made it challenging for him to concentrate on the intricacies and details required in his cases. Colleagues have observed that he seems less confident and more hesitant than usual, traits uncharacteristic of John's typically assertive demeanor. The trauma has also affected his sleep patterns. Nightmares involving scenes of police brutality are frequent, leaving John feeling physically and emotionally drained when he wakes up. He avoids dark or isolated areas and frequently checks the locks on their home doors at night. This heightened state of vigilance and fear disrupts any sense of normalcy in his daily life. Moreover, John experiences intense anxiety in situations that remind him of the incident. Crowded public spaces now feel overwhelming to him; he worries about potential confrontations or sudden outbreaks of violence, which leaves him feeling trapped and claustrophobic. He has begun avoiding social gatherings and outings with friends, citing fatigue as his reason for staying home. John's relationship with Sarah is also strained due to these changes. She notices his reluctance to engage in activities they once enjoyed together and feels helpless watching her husband suffer without understanding how she can support him better. John's preoccupation with the traumatic event has made it difficult for them to connect on a deeper level, leading to feelings of isolation and emotional distance between them. Despite his efforts to maintain professionalism at work, John struggles with decision-making processes and often second-guesses himself during trials. He questions whether he can ever truly be objective again after witnessing such an act of police violence up close. His once-strong belief in the justice system has been shaken, leaving him feeling disillusioned and unsure about his future in this field. John's story illustrates a profound shift from a man who was previously confident and dedicated to his role as a prosecutor, to someone now grappling with the aftermath of witnessing an act of police violence that has deeply impacted his personal and professional life.
